text:
cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg29.txt <<'EOF'
fix(codegen): a builtin's throwable names the line it was raised on

php reports the CALL SITE for a `TypeError` or `ValueError` a builtin raises — `fopen("", "r")` on
line 4 reports line 4 — because the builtin IS the frame; there is no internal one to name.
elephc's codegen-raised throwables carried no location at all:

    php:    Fatal error: Uncaught ValueError: Path must not be empty in p.php:4
    elephc: Fatal error: Uncaught ValueError: Path must not be empty

Every WARNING beside them already carried ` in FILE on line N`, and a user `throw` carried its
line, so the gap was exactly the builtin refusals — and `getLine()` answered 0 for a caught one.

The reason was written into the emitter: "Most codegen-raised throwables have no user `new` behind
them … so they carry no location, and PHP would name the internal call site anyway." That premise
is what measuring disproves. MEASURED across five raising sites — an empty path, a stream
`TypeError` through a `mixed`, `stream_filter_remove()` on a closed stream, `intdiv($a, 0)`, and a
user `throw` — php names the user's line every time.

`emit_static_exception_at` could already take a location and `new $c(...)` passed one; every other
emitter called the `None` wrapper. Rather than thread `inst` through several dozen call sites, the
context already knows which instruction is being lowered, so `current_source_location()` derives it
there and every emitter picks it up. A module with no source path, or an instruction with no span,
still produces the previous bare wording.

`emit_closed_stream_type_error` needed more than that: it HAND-ROLLED the throw machinery — the
same allocation, heap kind, class id, message pair, zero code, `_exc_value` publish and
`__rt_throw_current` jump the shared emitter performs — and the one thing it left out was the
creation line. A duplicate of that machinery could only ever drift from it, so it now calls
`exceptions::emit_type_error` and the copy goes.

Both halves are pinned: `getLine()` on a caught throwable and the ` in FILE:LINE` suffix on the
uncaught report read the same slot, so a test for only one would let an emitter that fills the slot
and forgets the suffix — or the reverse — pass.
EOF
